 OsamaSon concert in NYC ends in chaos and reported injuries
 DJ Nino Andretti allegedly told fans to “rush the merch booth” at the end of last night’s concert, leading to serious injuries.
 By Vivian Medithi , Logan Lacy 
 November 20, 2026
 Share -->
 Tweet -->
 OsamaSon performing at First Class Fest 2026 in Toronto this August.
 Joshua Kaufman / First Class Fest
 Last night, OsamaSon played a show in New York City at Terminal 5 for Nike's Jordan brand that appears to have spiraled into chaos. 
 In a statement to XXL, NYPD said they arrived to a “disorderly” crowd exiting the premises and that “four individuals sustained minor injuries. EMS transported two individuals to the hospital in stable condition, while the remaining to refused medical attention in the scene.” No arrests have been made.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Read Next:
 Watch OsamaSon talk mental health and his creative process in a new FADER doc
 Video footage and photos uploaded to on social media last night appear to show a serious crowd crush, with reports of broken limbs, flooding, and near-death situations, according to concert goers. According to posts on X and TikTok, attendees said that the chaos was allegedly caused after OsamaSon’s DJ, Nino Andretti, told fans to “rush the merch booth” near the close of his set. 
 "almost died tn @ osamason in nyc.. i know i be over exaggerating and shit but being crushed under 2 people and seeing the guy under me completely unconscious mightve actually traumatized me," reads one post on X by the user @elonsmdnicca . 
 Another video circulating on X and TikTok capturing the concert shows a pile of attendees collapsed on top of one another, with one repeatedly screaming "help." Photos also show attendees being carried out of the venue to an ambulance on a stretcher . 
 More footage from the crush / stampede after the Osamason show in New York City at Terminal 5 https://t.co/pttY6MgE0Y
— TruScene (@TruSceneIG) November 20, 2026 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 A representative for OsamaSon said they did not have a statement about the night. Representatives for Terminal 5 did not immediately respond to requests for comment at press time.
 A reported crowd crush at Terminal 5 in NYC after an Osamason show left multiple people injured. Fans say the DJ allegedly said to rush to the merch room for an “exclusive gift,” triggering a surge through the main hallway that turned into a stampede. https://t.co/njwRmkvlCm
— Breaking911 (@Breaking911) November 20, 2026 
 The FADER's interns Logan Lacy and photographer Narayan Naidu were at the concert and shared a firsthand account of their experience. Naidu said that several fans had passed out even before Andretti’s set, and that a busted water pipe and pulled fire alarm only exacerbated the chaos at the tail end of the concert.
 Logan and Naidu arrived at Terminal 5 around 7:30 p.m. on Thursday evening. Doors were at 7 p.m., so the line was already wrapped around the block. Lacy recalls that by 8:20 p.m. or so, fans were already stepping out of the crowd due to the intensity of the DJ set.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 "I knew it was going to be a crazy show when 15 minutes into the DJ set, dude comes out with a with a cup of water, absolutely soaked. Just sits down looking like he saw the light," Lacy said. "It was the craziest thing ever: his face was pale. He was just wet, drenched. Sat down, put his head down, like sitting in the fetal position. It was like what in the world, right?"
 Shortly after, another fan emerged missing one of his Uggs, also during the DJ set ahead of OsamaSon's performance. OsamaSon went onstage around 9:15 p.m., slightly ahead of schedule, and Lacy says that from what he observed from the photo pit in front of the barricade, it was clear that the fans at the front of the crowd couldn't move. After three songs, Lacy ventured into the crowd, starting from the back and moving forward by swimming "like a fish." At one point, a large pit opened up and he took the opportunity to move up into the center front of the crowd.
 By this point, Lacy says, every song generated its own mosh pit, to the point that the crowd knocked him over at one point. "It was complete just craziness. You look to your left and you look to your right and people look like they've been hit with tear gas or something," Lacy said. "Their eyes barely open, mouths wide open, like they were on autopilot. It was like nothing was there."
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Zaid (@z3id___) 
 Lacy says despite the intensity of the moshpits and the usual errant elbows, OsamaSon's fans were generally pretty kind to each other.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 "I will say there was a huge sense of camaraderie because so many people fell and people were actually trying to help them up," says Lacy. "Mo one got stampeded or anything, but I had to help 4 people up – that is a record for me. Every song – there were no breaks, no water, no breaks in the in the set, just onto the next song, just keep it going, keep it going, keep it going. And it eventually got a lot tamer towards the end because people were just like, you know, it was just suffocating, but there were still subsections – like I could hear people behind me screaming every song."
 All of this came to a head near the end of OsamaSon's set, when DJ Nino Andretti encouraged fans to "rush" the merch booth. Per Lacy:
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by @tmp.eli 
 The DJ comes out and says, 'Everybody rush the merch, we got a surprise for you.' Boom, half the crowd just bounces. DJ performs his own Osamason song [...] After, he like, doubles down. He'd already tripled down at this point, but he like quadruples down and says, 'what are you guys still doing here? Rush the merch right now.'
 So after this, you know, everyone goes over to the merch. Obviously I decided that is a terrible idea, but I do walk past and it was insane. I couldn't see, it was just a wall of people, and obviously it was a lot of screaming, a lot of shouting, it was just utter chaos.[...] then the fire alarm goes off.
 Come to find out a pipe burst, like a water pipe burst. There was water gushing somewhere in the venue. So the fire alarm goes off and now security is pressing people, telling them like, 'get the fuck out.'
 Outside, Lacy says he and Naidu saw a girl sobbing outside, saying her friend was "hurt really bad." Lacy says that friend apparently "snapped his ankle," and that he witnessed two other fans help him onto a stretcher after an ambulance arrived.
